generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

  1. How is the Logarithmic function \(y = \log_a x\) defined?

    The logarithmic function \(y = \log_a x\) is defined as the inverse function of the exponential function \(y = a^x\), where \(a\) is the base of the logarithm.

    In other words, the logarithmic function undoes what the exponential function does.

    It is defined as for \(x>0 ,\,a>0\) and \(a \neq 1,\)

    \(y = \log_a x \Leftrightarrow a^y=x\)

  2. For the logarithmic function \(y = \log_a x\):

    1. \(\text{Dom}(y)\): The domain of \(y\) in this function consists of all positive real numbers greater than \(0\), because the argument \(x\) must be a positive real number. In interval notation, it can be represented as \((0, +\infty)\).
    2. \(\text{Range}(y) \): The range of \(y\) in this function includes all real numbers, because the result \(y\) can be any real number. In interval notation, it can be represented as \((-\infty, +\infty)\).

  3. Here is the sketch of the graph of \(y = \log_a x\) if \(a>1\)

    [[jsxgraph]] var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [-2, 7, 10, -7], keepaspectratio: false, showCopyright: false, axis: true, grid: true, showNavigation: false }); // Define slider for the base a var slider = board.create('slider', [[1, 4], [3, 4], [1.1, {#a_cor#}, {#a_cor+1#}]], { name: 'a', snapWidth: 0.1, withLabel: true, fixed: false }); function loga(x) { var a = slider.Value(); return Math.log(x) / Math.log(a); } // Draw the logarithmic function y = log_a(x) var logGraph = board.create('functiongraph', [loga, 0.01, 8.9], { strokeColor: 'blue', strokeWidth: 2, name: 'y = log_a(x),a>1 ', withLabel: true, label: { position: 'rt', offset: [-10, -10] }, fixed: true }); // Draw the vertical asymptote at x = 0 var asymptote = board.create('line', [[0, -6.7], [0, 6.6]], { straightFirst: false, straightLast: false, strokeColor: 'red', dash: 2, fixed: true }); // Highlight the point (1, 0) on the graph var point = board.create('glider', [{#x_cord#}, {#y_cord#}, logGraph], { name: '\\(({#x_cord#}, {#y_cord#})\\)', size: 4, face: 'o', strokeColor: 'green', fillColor: 'green', fixed: true }); // Update the graph and the point when the slider is moved slider.on('drag', function() { logGraph.Y = loga; point.moveTo([{#x_cord#}, {#y_cord#}]); board.update(); }); [[/jsxgraph]]

This question delves into the peculiar nature of logarithmic functions with a base of 1, examining their definition and characteristics. It explores the domain and range of the function \( y = \log_{1}x \) and provides insights into its graph. Additionally, it sketches the general shape of the graph of logarithmic functions \( y = \log_{a}x \) when \( a > 1 \).
